message.content:
A modern out-of-order superscalar CPU is a machine that tries to execute many instructions per cycle while preserving the illusion of a simple, in-order, sequentially consistent program. It does this by separating the *architectural* view of the program from the *microarchitectural* execution machinery. Instructions are fetched, decoded, renamed, scheduled, executed out of order, and then retired in program order. The pipeline is filled with prediction, speculation, buffering, and dependency tracking so that the processor can hide latency and exploit instruction-level parallelism.

Below is a detailed technical walkthrough.

---

# 1. High-Level Pipeline View

A simplified modern x86-64 or ARM64 out-of-order core may look like this:

```text
Fetch
  |
  v
Branch Prediction / Fetch Control
  |
  v
Instruction Cache / ITLB
  |
  v
Decode / Micro-op Generation
  |
  v
Rename / Allocate
  |
  v
Dispatch / Issue Queue Allocation
  |
  v
Scheduler / Issue
  |
  v
